_tuning_notes: Spawn rarity presets, calibrated against vanilla's own jungle pool (parrot 40 / chicken 10 / ocelot 2 / panda 1). A species picks ONE tier name and inherits weight + group size + nearby_cap; explicit weight/group_size/nearby_cap in a species file still win. nearby_cap is the accumulation killer: CREATURE-category animals never despawn, so without a cap a modest weight piles up forever (this is how gorillas reached ~30x panda density). attempt_chance thins epic tiers further — only that fraction of otherwise-valid spawn attempts survive. Hot-reloadable: edit + /reload and density changes with no rebuild. DENSITY 0.4.5: the whole ladder scaled 2.5x (ubiquitous 12->30, common 8->20, uncommon 4->10, rare 2->5, epic 1->2). Scaling the WHOLE ladder matters: bumping only the two tiers in use left uncommon(10) above common(8), i.e. a tier named 'common' rarer than one named 'uncommon'. spawn-lint now enforces monotonicity. The 0.4.0 cut to panda-class was right about runaway accumulation but overshot discoverability — players could cross a pregenerated world and meet one animal. nearby_cap is untouched and still bounds local density, so this raises how often you MEET an animal without letting a biome silt up. Raising a weight above the value baked at world load needs a restart; lowering is live on /reload.
